messages.subject: profiling tools?
parts:
What profiling tools for g++ compiled code
should I use? There seem to be dozens available.

I know Matt suggested something ages ago, but
neither Daniel nor I can fish it out of our email.

(The context is we're trying to verify that the
problem Jiqiang's having with autocorrelation is not
due to Stan. I don't see any way Stan could be as
slow as what Jiqiang reports, so I'm guessing it's
something ugly in the R/C++ glue.)

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] profiling tools?
parts:
I've used kcachegrind under Linux with good success.  You compile the program per normal (with debugging symbols) and then run it under valgrind and process the results with kcachegrind to explore where time is being spent.  It gives line-by-line breakdowns, call stacks, etc

I've also used gprof a bit, but I find it clunky and tedious to parse the results with the kinds of call stacks we tend to have in stan.

Cheers,
Marcus
